scenarios.name: with-cleric-creature-dies-drains
scenarios.why: Seat 0 controls a Cleric, so Relic Vial has the granted trigger; a creature seat 0 controls dying makes the opponent lose 1 and seat 0 gain 1.

scenarios.name: without-cleric-no-drain
scenarios.why: No Cleric: Relic Vial has no triggered ability, so a creature dying changes no life total.

scenarios.name: cleric-cast-this-turn-grant-is-live-at-once
scenarios.why: The grant is not locked in: the moment a Cleric (Harsh Mentor, cast this turn) is on the battlefield, the next creature death drains.

scenarios.name: only-cleric-dies-looks-back
scenarios.why: "Whenever a creature you control dies" is a leaves-the-battlefield trigger and looks back in time: when the only Cleric itself dies, Relic Vial had the ability immediately before the event, so it triggers.

scenarios.name: only-cleric-dies-to-damage-looks-back
scenarios.why: Triage control (added after the destroy variant failed; expectation is CR-only): the only Cleric dying to lethal damage, a state-based action, is the same look-back case and must drain.

scenarios.name: sacrifice-only-cleric-as-cost-looks-back
scenarios.why: Triage control (CR-only expectation): sacrificing the only Cleric to Relic Vial's own ability is a death the game looks back on, so the granted trigger drains; the ability also draws a card.
